capabilities: Stamp authorship frontmatter fields (created_by, last_modified_by, edit_count, content_origin) when you type
Append section-level change summaries to a daily JSONL log
Attribute files created in mapped auto-import folders to a configured source and trust level
Classify content trust using suggested content_origin values such as primary or ai-generated
Query the provenance fields with Dataview
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. README documents privacy guarantees (no network requests, no telemetry, no runtime dependencies) and known limitations: no retroactive attribution, content_origin fixed at creation, regex pattern screening is not a sandbox, log pruning only runs at startup, and disabling the plugin drops pending edits.
problem: In vaults where humans, AI assistants, and scripts all edit notes, every note looks the same, so you cannot tell who wrote a note or how much to trust its content.

relations.evidence: Because everything is plain frontmatter, you can query it with Dataview

summary: Provenance tracker that stamps authorship frontmatter fields on edited notes and keeps a daily JSONL log of who changed what.
